summary: Nora Kershaw Chadwick worked in history, archaeology, and linguistics. After studying at Newnham College (1911–1915), she held posts at the University of St Andrews (1919–1923) and the University of Cambridge (1950–1958).

Norbert M. Samuelson worked in philosophy and religious studies. He studied at Northwestern University, Hebrew Union College, and Indiana University under Shlomo Pines. He held faculty positions at Temple University (1975–1998) and Arizona State University.

Noriaki Hakamaya specializes in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He studied at Komazawa University and the University of Tokyo under Shun'ei Hirai and Zuiho Yamaguchi. He served as professor at Komazawa University (1985–2011) and Komazawa Junior College (1994–2006).

Noriaki Hosoda works in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. His career includes posts as assistant (attested 1986) and associate professor (attested 2003) at Hokkaido University, and professor at Kyoto Bunkyo University (attested 2026).
Noriaki Inoue is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Taisho University until 1953, where he later served as professor (attested 1982).

Norihiko Tanaka specializes in Buddhist studies. He studied at Osaka Kyoiku University, Bukkyo University, and Visva-Bharati University. He served Bukkyo University as lecturer, associate professor, professor (1994, 2013), and professor emeritus (2015–2021).
Norihiko Uchida worked in linguistics and Indology. He studied under Yutaka Ochihara and held an assistant post at Osaka University of Foreign Studies, attested in 1962.
Norihiro Matsuura works in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Sinology. Matsuura is attested in 2026 as a faculty member at Otani University and the Otani Academic Society.

Norihisa Baba specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. Educated at Hanazono University and the University of Tokyo under Masahiro Shimoda, he has held academic appointments at the University of Tokyo and its Institute for Advanced Studies on Asia.
Norio Koyama works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Shinshu University and under Seitatsu Matsunami, later serving as professor at Taisho University (attested 2014).

Noritoshi Aramaki is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. Educated at Kyoto University, he served as associate professor at Kyoto University and Osaka University, and as professor at Kyoto University (2000) and Otani University (2000–2007).

Noriyuki Kudo specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. After postgraduate studies at Bukkyo University, where he also lectured (attested 1999–2000), he served as associate professor at Soka University (attested 2000–2026).

Norman Fischer works in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at Colgate University, the University of Iowa, UC Berkeley, and the Graduate Theological Union, trained under Mel Weitsman and Richard Baker, and founded the Everyday Zen Foundation in 2000.

Norman Mosley Penzer was a scholar in Indology and other fields. In 1925, he was attested as a Fellow of the Royal Anthropological Institute, Royal Geographical Society, and Geological Society, and as a member of the Folklore and Royal Asiatic societies.

Norvin J. Hein was a scholar of Indology and religious studies. He studied under Franklin Edgerton and served as Associate Professor of Comparative Religion in the Divinity School at Yale University, attested in 1965.

Nosei Fuji specializes in Buddhist studies. He studied at Dongguk University and held appointments at Daegu University, Kyushu Ryukoku Junior College, and Ryukoku University, where he was professor of Buddhist studies (attested 2011–2013).

Notto R. Thelle works in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Japanology. He served as associate director at the NCC Center for the Study of Japanese Religions in 1974 and held a post at the University of Oslo from 1986 to 2006.

Noémie Verdon works in Indology and Iranian and Central Asian studies. She completed her PhD at the University of Lausanne in 2015 under Johannes Bronkhorst and Charles Genequand, and later held a post at Kyoto University (attested 2018–2019).

Noël Peri worked in Japanology, Buddhist studies, and Sinology. He taught Western music at Tokyo University of the Arts (1896–1906) and served as a resident and secretary-librarian at the École française d'Extrême-Orient starting in 1907 and 1911.

Nyanaponika Thera was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Nyanatiloka Mahathera, Mahasi Sayadaw, and at the University of Ceylon. He co-founded the Buddhist Publication Society, serving as its leader, editor (1958–1984), and president (1958–1988).
